tagline: The physical debut of a new brand identity. The first time Fender Studio met the industry face to face, on the floor in Anaheim.
facts: Anaheim Convention Center · The NAMM Show

p: NAMM 2026 was the public debut of Fender Studio: the identity that carries PreSonus into the larger Fender organization.

The booth had one job. Launch broad brand awareness for that transition, and make the new identity's first physical impression land with the industry. Everything on the floor, from the buildout to the screens to the print, was in service of that debut.

blocks.p: A trade show floor is an unforgiving first impression. The identity had to read from across the hall, hold up at arm's length, and stay consistent from the screens to the signage to the card in someone's hand.

p: LED wall graphic assets, overlays, and layouts, built to carry the Fender Studio system across the booth's largest surface. The wall cycled brand moments, product features, and live content through the show.

items: LED wall running Fender Studio brand content at NAMM 2026
LED wall running Fender Studio product content at NAMM 2026

blocks.lede: The wall did not just run graphics. We programmed the booth as a live stage and cut the sessions for distribution, so the debut kept working long after the doors closed in Anaheim.

items.title: DJ Jazzy Jeff
items.desc: The headline draw. A keynote set from a hall-of-fame DJ, staged inside the booth and packaged for YouTube to pull the debut well past the floor.

items.title: Joey Burcham
items.desc: Roo Studios owner and engineer, demonstrating the workflow to a room of dealers and working professionals. The credibility layer.

items.title: Josh Cumbee
items.desc: Producer and songwriter session, showing the software in the hands of a working writer rather than on a spec sheet.

p: The floor is four days. The work around it runs longer: social graphics building awareness before the doors opened, and print that stayed in someone's hand after they walked away.

p: The booth marked the public debut of Fender Studio, a newly minted subbrand transitioning the PreSonus identity into the larger Fender organization. The goal was brand awareness for that transition, and the booth was where the new identity met the industry for the first time. Across four days on the floor it drew dealers, press, and A-list musical talent, all meeting the brand in person for the first time.
